inputs.text: Lower courts have ruled that schools can ban wearing apparel that can reasonably be interpreted as profane. The case involving two Michigan middle-school brothers who were told to remove their hoodies emblazoned with the phrase “Let’s Go Brandon” is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The siblings are being represented by the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, which states that the boys’ school violated their First Amendment rights. The phrase gained popularity during a 2021 NASCAR event when a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” while an NBC interviewer told racer Brandon Brown that they were yelling “Let’s go Brandon!” A judge...
